steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Leadership is a central theme: Caesar presents himself as the ideal Roman general — decisive, brave, and always in control. Contrast this with Tacitus's portrait of weak or tyrannical emperors. | Key Fact: Roman imperialism: Caesar justifies conquest as bringing civilisation and order to barbarians; Tacitus questions whether empire brings freedom or oppression. | Key Fact: Virtus (manly courage/excellence) is a key Roman value: in Caesar it means military bravery; in Cicero it means moral courage to defend the Republic. | Key Fact: Pietas (duty to gods, country, and family) drives Roman heroes but can also create conflict: duty to the state vs personal loyalty.
